key_insight: CORAL improves medical report generation by combining lesion localization with clinically defined concept reasoning inside a multimodal language model.
clinical_relevance: This approach aims to make automated imaging reports more interpretable and more aligned with the structured evidence-based workflow used in clinical diagnosis.
method: Prompt-driven segmentation localizes lesions in the image.
A Concept Bottleneck module predicts multi-class clinical attributes.
Concept tokens and mask-modulated visual features are fused in an MLLM to generate structured reports and diagnostic predictions.
evidence_signal: On BUS-CoT and IU X-ray, the method showed better diagnostic accuracy, concept consistency, and report quality than strong general-purpose and medical MLLMs.
watch_item: Performance and interpretability may depend on accurate lesion localization and reliable concept supervision, which can be harder to obtain across imaging settings.
paper_title: Concept-Grounded Reasoning with Prompt-Driven Localization for Interpretable Structured Report Generation
